title: Computational Arbitrage in AI Model Markets

validation_policy.learned_preprocessing: fit on training only; apply frozen fitted transforms to validation/test
validation_policy.instance_roles: Preserve explicit per-instance observation/training/calibration/causal-feedback roles; no evaluation-target fitting or validation-derived fitted state carried across independent cases.
validation_policy.enforcement: binding prompt and task contract; task-specific replay/guards where available; arbitrary training-data provenance requires source/patch audit

research_contract.objective: Reduce the expected cost, in USD scaled to the 500-issue benchmark, of buying a 70% solve rate on SWE-bench Verified issues unseen in fitting, from the paper's two-model market.
fixed_research_objects: The market: GPT-5 mini and DeepSeek v3.2 Thinking only, with the authors' released per-issue attempts and mean costs. No other model may be bought.
The purchase rule: repeated sampling until first success, at most $1 per issue, each model used at most once per issue, per-model outcomes treated as independent (paper Eq. 8).
The estimators: unbiased pass@k from attempts, k = floor(dollars / mean_cost), expected spend by the survival identity, computed by the trusted scorer from outcomes it holds.
The target and scale: 70% solve rate read from the lower convex envelope of a nested purchase family, mean cost multiplied by 500.
Generalization: outcomes of evaluation issues stay hidden; inputs are only fields known before buying (problem statement, repo, version).
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
editable_components: The purchase policy as a whole: the fixed-tau cascade is a baseline choice, not a requirement. Per-issue or per-repo allocation, model order, skipping issues, budget levels and the split between models may all change.

Anything fitted at train stage from data/train: predictors of solve probability or cost built on problem statements, repo and version, any model class and objective, with dependencies from PyPI in env.lock.

When retaining the supplied issue-independent cascade, changing only the model order gpt5mini then deepseek, the fitted cap of $0.0812, budget_levels=logspace(1e-4, 1, 250), performance_grid=linspace(0.68, max_perf, 1000) or compute_first=logspace(0.01, 0.5, 100) does not count as a method improvement.
forbidden_substitutions: Buying from any model outside the two-model market, changing the $1 cap, the estimators, the 70% target or the 500-issue scale, or reporting cost or solve figures instead of plans.
Using outcomes, gold patches, test lists or per-issue results of benchmark issues from memory or outside sources, or embedding per-issue tables for issues outside data/train.
Training or fitting reusable model state or learned preprocessing on validation features or labels, including final train+val refits or validation-based distillation.

evidence.section: Sections 2 and 3, Figure 1, Figure 2, Eq. 7 and 8
evidence.finding: Buy cost at a target solve rate in the GPT-5 mini and DeepSeek market is the headline experiment; the cascade with tau is the paper's simple policy, with the policy class left open by Eq. 6.
Trusted replay holds attempts and mean costs and takes only plans from the candidate.
The scorer reproduces the authors' $78.74 on all 445 issues without the envelope.

split.decision: The paper has no split: it fits and reports on one set of 445 SWE-bench Verified issues. Disjoint train, val and held-out issues, stratified by repo, 50/20/30, drawn once with secrets; the record stays under the judge directory. Only a baseline that cannot reach 70% may trigger a redraw; none happened.

baseline.paper_ref: Figure 1 and Section 3: $80 buy cost at a 75% solve rate, tau* = {$0.08, $0.92}; reproduced $78.74. Parity through this task's scorer on all 445 issues with the authors' tau* = {$0.0812, $0.9188}: authors' code $78.7367, scorer without the envelope $78.7327 (difference -$0.0040, -0.005%), scorer with the envelope $77.8836 (-$0.85, the chord between levels 228 and 230 under a non-convex step). DeepSeek alone at 75%: authors' code $118.445, scorer without the envelope $118.465. See judge/verification/parity_75.json. This task's metric is at 70% on held-out issues, so its value differs from those.
baseline.timing_scope: train_min and eval_min are conservative estimates before the first reference; NOTES section 5 has what was measured.
